walkthroughs.body_html:
Paper 2: Drama — a core area of GCSE English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Paper 2: Drama brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Paper 2: Drama.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the dramatic function of a soliloquy?
options: A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
It means it is wrong to write fiction.
A soliloquy is any long speech a character gives.
It reveals a character's inner thoughts directly to the audience while the character is alone on stage — a convention granting access to private psychology.
Dramatic irony is when characters speak in dramatic voices.
A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
When the audience knows something a character does not, creating tension between the character's words/actions and the audience's understanding.
Dramatic irony is when something ironic happens in a play.
It means authors can never make mistakes when writing.
The claim that judging a text by what the author 'intended' is fallacious — the text's meaning lies in the work itself, not the author's stated or guessed intentions.
Dramatic irony is when characters speak in dramatic voices.
It means it is wrong to write fiction.
